audit.why: Lane difficulty is accurately framed: early is Malzahar-favoured via Q silence + E perma-shove, mid flips at first item, teamfights favour Vladimir's AoE over his single pick. EVEN 5.5/10 matches the 48.2% WR over 4147 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart shows 'Skill' for rows 0-5 while the content layer and packet both show Malzahar for Levels 1-6 and Vladimir from first item — two different answers rendered to the user.
audit.why: Content win[] and packet levelChart agree (Malzahar 0-4, Vladimir 5-6); the full layer carries a blanket 'Skill'. Content layer is already correct, so side edits alone plus rewritten whys, per the chart rule.
audit.corrected: phases[0-4].side -> Malzahar, phases[5].side -> Vladimir, whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no numbers; dos/donts bodies were tradeGood/tradeBad pasted under unrelated titles.
audit.why: Nether Grasp is 140/110/80s and Call of the Void is a flat 6s — the numbers that make 'wait for cooldown' advice concrete. Pool cannot break the suppression once it lands (existing text says this correctly in spikes).
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns inserted; bullet bodies rewritten to match their titles.

audit.whatIsWrong: Malefic Visions execute-threshold pressure (missingInteractions) was not stated anywhere.
audit.why: E is a DoT that passes on kill; charging your own E at low HP inside his range hands him the DoT kill. Folded into dontsFull[2].d.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[2].d now names the self-damage-into-Visions risk.

edits.before: - Malzahar Nether Grasp: matchup-defining — Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Sanguine Pool has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Nether Grasp is 140s at rank 1, 80 at rank 3 — point-and-click suppression; never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. - Call of the Void silence cycles on a flat 6s. - Your W Sanguine Pool has one job: the gank that follows his R. Your R has one too: the kill.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, E-charge as he steps to answer, release and walk — the trade costs him HP and pays yours.
edits.after: Hold W for the gank that follows his R, not for poke — once Nether Grasp lands, pool cannot break it.

edits.before: Pooling his poke and then eating the real engage at half HP with nothing — the pool is a combo-breaker, not a flinch reflex.
edits.after: Charging E costs your own health inside his 900-range Q — at half HP that self-damage feeds a Malefic Visions kill.

edits.before: Q-farm and nothing else — your level 1 is among the worst mid. Give CS you can't Q safely and smile about it.
edits.after: His silence and Visions bully one of the worst level 1s mid — Q-farm, give CS you can't take safely, and hold.

edits.before: Still surviving. Q on cooldown when free, pool saved for the jungler you haven't seen yet.
edits.after: His as he layers Q silence into push — Q-farm when free, pool saved for the jungler.

edits.before: E charges join the pattern: Q-E wave contact trades start mattering. Health is your mana — spend like an accountant.
edits.after: Full perma-shove online keeps him ahead — E-Q wave contact is your only answer; spend health like an accountant.

edits.before: The crimson rush timing — Q empowers every third-ish cast and the sustain war starts tilting your way.
edits.after: Still his — pinned under tower and gank-vulnerable, though empowered Q starts tilting the sustain war.

edits.before: Hemoplague online — the all-in inverts: Q-E-R-E with ignite kills most mids who thought they were winning.
edits.after: His 6 beats yours — Nether Grasp is point-and-click and pool cannot break it, so no solo all-in with R up.

edits.before: Riftmaker timing: every trade heals more than it costs. Extended fights are now donations to your health bar.
edits.after: First item flips it — Riftmaker trades heal more than they cost; extended fights become donations to you.
